chunks: As for what Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim and others, from Abū ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام, that he said:

There is no harm in going ahead from Minā to ʿArafāt before sunrise, and in going ahead from al-Muzdalifah to Minā so that they stone the jamarāt and perform salat al-fajr in their lodgings at Minā, there is no harm. The proper way regarding this report is that we understand it as applying to one who has excuses, such as the sick person, women, the menstruating woman, and other such excuses. But when the excuse has ceased, then it is not permissible, according to what we have stated before; that is indicated by this.

key_terms.التَّقَدُّمِ: going ahead or departing earlier than the usual time
key_terms.الْأَعْذَارِ: legally recognized excuses that justify an exception
key_terms.الْحَائِضِ: the menstruating woman included among those with excuses
key_terms.الْمَرِيضِ: the sick person whose condition warrants concession
key_terms.الْمُزْدَلِفَةِ: the hajj station where pilgrims stay before proceeding to Minā
key_terms.مِنًى: the sacred site of the hajj rites where stoning the jamarāt takes place
key_terms.يَرْمُونَ الْجِمَارَ: they perform the ritual stoning of the jamarāt

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to leave al-Muzdalifah for Minā before fajr during hajj?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling on departing early during the rites of hajj, specifically moving from al-Muzdalifah to Minā before dawn. It explains that such early departure is to be understood as permitted for those with valid excuses, such as illness or women with specific circumstances, while it is not allowed once the excuse no longer applies.
